targets.writeCondition: Runs after 'Get NonWorkingDays' -> 'Update LastThreeWorkingDays Variable' (Success constraints DTSX:4551-4552). One Update per transfer request WHERE gen_tanferinstatus = 7 AND gen_SendToBankDate IS NOT NULL AND datediff(day, ?, gen_SendToBankDate) <= 0 (DTSX:3584-3587), ? = User::LastThreeWorkingDays (ParameterMapping DTSX:3592 -> variable DTSX:20), i.e. send-to-bank date (date part, as stored, no time-zone conversion in the SQL) on or before LastThreeWorkingDays. LastThreeWorkingDays is computed by Script Task 'Update LastThreeWorkingDays Variable' (ScriptMain.cs:107-135): starting from DateTime.Now.AddDays(-1).Date it walks back day by day, skipping days present in User::NonWorkingDays (CalendarRule starttime of 'Friday'/'Saturday'/'Holiday' rules within the last 21 days, Execute SQL DTSX:2260-2261), and returns the 3rd working day counting yesterday as the 1st. Rows whose SDK call throws are redirected to the Error output, which has no path (paths DTSX:4541-4542) - silently discarded.

unresolved.reason: Update LastThreeWorkingDays Variable ScriptMain.cs:121 matches non-working days with dt.Select("starttime = '" + currDate.ToString() + "'"): currDate is local midnight formatted with the runtime culture, while CalendarRule.starttime is read as stored (the SQL compares it against GetutcDate()). Whether these values ever match (and therefore whether Fridays/Saturdays/holidays are really skipped) depends on server culture, time zone and CalendarRule data - not determinable from the DTSX.

Excluded as ETL plumbing: End ETL Process record\ETL Record Finish (updates gen_etlprocess, main.cs:120-129). Also plumbing (control flow): Create ETL Process record (gen_etlprocess create, ScriptMain.cs:47-52), Get Variables From Etl Variables. No event handlers in this package.

The Script Task here differs textually from the one in 0027_AutomatedJoining (counter starts at 2 and counts down to 0, ScriptMain.cs:111-129, versus 1 counting up to 3 in 0027) but yields the same date: the 3rd working day back, counting yesterday as the 1st.

Update LastThreeWorkingDays Variable ScriptMain.cs:96-104: on exception the catch sets TaskResult = Failure but line 104 unconditionally sets Success afterwards, so the package continues and User::LastThreeWorkingDays keeps its previous value (design-time value '10/3/2017 1:52:22 PM', DTSX:20; the package defines no package configurations - only a job-level override (e.g. /SET) could change it, which is outside the DTSX). In that case the cut-off date would be 2017-10-03.
The attribute logical name is spelled 'gen_tanferinstatus' (sic) both in the SQL (DTSX:3586) and in the code (main.cs:121); recorded exactly as written.
